summary: The article accurately reports on the withdrawal of IGST exemption and the introduction of a new customs levy on precious metal imports, with correct dates and percentages. However, it misrepresents the nature of the "new 3% customs levy" as distinct from IGST.

claims.claim: The Indian government has withdrawn the upfront IGST exemption for banks and nominated agencies importing precious metals.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the withdrawal of the upfront IGST exemption for banks and nominated agencies importing precious metals.

claims.claim: A new 3% customs levy has also been introduced on these precious metal imports since April 1, 2026.
claims.note: Sources indicate that the 3% is IGST that banks now have to pay upfront, not a new *customs levy* in addition to existing customs duties. The article conflates the withdrawal of IGST exemption with a new customs levy.

claims.claim: This 3% levy is over and above any existing basic customs duties (BCD) that may already apply to these metals. For instance, if basic customs duty on gold is 15%, this new 3% levy would be an additional charge on the import value, further increasing the landed cost of the metal.
claims.note: The 3% is IGST, which is a separate tax from customs duties. While it adds to the upfront cost, it's not an *additional customs levy* on top of BCD. The article incorrectly presents it as an additional customs levy.

claims.claim: Since April 1, 2026, these importers must pay IGST upfront when bringing these precious metals into the country.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that banks and nominated agencies are required to pay 3% IGST upfront on precious metal imports effective April 1, 2026.

claims.claim: In May, the government had also hiked import duty on gold and silver to 15%, from 6%, and on platinum to 15.4%, from 6.4%, to curb non-essential imports.
claims.note: Several sources confirm that the import duty on gold and silver was hiked to 15% (from 6%) and on platinum to 15.4% (from 6.4%) in May 2026.

article_title: Gold, Silver, Platinum Import Tax Relief Ends: What It Means for Buyers
